For modern games, a big problem is performance. Split screen basically means you have to render two copies of the same game, from two different camera viewpoints, on the same hardware. On a console capped to 30fps and let's be generous and say textures made for 720p quality: not a big problem to have split screen, it means the console needs to render 60fps for twice as many of those 720p textures. On a PC, where players expect 60fps and 1080p-quality textures at minimum, a split screen would mean 120fps rendered and again, twice as many textured objects (now with higher quality textures) to keep track of. And god forbid if you're running 144Hz monitor with 2K quality. Putting that on a split screen is again: twice the frames per second, and twice as many textured objects to keep track of.
